old_text: The indices in Figure~\ref{fig:tiers} mix two effects: how good a placement is, and how the classifier that produced it prices interference. To separate them, the final placement of every simulation repetition is re-scored twice over the full 120-sample trace: once by the configuration's own classifier (self) and once by the full-fingerprint classifier as a common reference (oracle), with ten repetitions per configuration (Figure~\ref{fig:oracle}). Both scores use the same window, so they differ only in the classifier; because they score the final placement over the whole trace instead of averaging the scheduler's analysis intervals, which include the unoptimized initial placement, they differ from the indices of Figure~\ref{fig:tiers}: lower for canonical-7 and full-fingerprint, and slightly higher for proxy-swap (3817 against 3619). The canonical-7 classifier is pessimistic about its own placements: the reference prices them 20\% lower (paired difference $-967$, 95\% CI $-1047$ to $-894$). The proxy-swap classifier is slightly optimistic: the reference prices its placements 4\% higher ($+162$, CI $+58$ to $+283$). The full-fingerprint scores coincide by construction, which checks the re-scoring path. On the full-fingerprint reference, canonical-7 and proxy-swap placements are statistically indistinguishable (3844 versus 3979; difference $+135$, CI $-149$ to $+421$, Welch $p=0.39$)\oldval{earlier wording: ``On the common reference'', before the other two references were run}. Full-fingerprint placements score lower than both (3607; $-237$ versus canonical-7, CI $-421$ to $-68$; $-372$ versus proxy-swap, CI $-629$ to $-138$), but that comparison favours the full fingerprint by construction, since its search optimized against the same classifier that serves as the reference. Repeating the re-score with the canonical-7 and the proxy-swap classifiers as the reference, in two further batches of ten repetitions each (the simulator is unseedable, so each batch produces its own placements), shows that no ordering survives the change: each reference ranks its own configuration first in point estimate. On the canonical-7 reference, proxy-swap placements score 936 above canonical-7 ones (CI $+604$ to $+1231$, Welch $p<0.001$) and full-fingerprint placements are indistinguishable from canonical-7 ($+90$, CI $-166$ to $+364$, $p=0.54$); on the proxy-swap reference the sign reverses, proxy-swap placements scoring 227 below canonical-7 ones (bootstrap CI $-434$ to $-21$ but Welch $p=0.057$, so the two tests disagree at this sample size; \tbd{S6}{permutation $p$ at $n=20$, Holm-corrected}) and full-fingerprint placements worst ($+1164$ versus proxy-swap, CI $+510$ to $+1995$). The full fingerprint's penalty under the two five-class references has a mechanical cause: its regime workload, which those references cannot express, is relabelled as plain CPU in every sample. At ten repetitions per cell, therefore, no reference-free ranking of these placements exists, and the preceding paragraph should be read as one column of that matrix (Figure~\ref{fig:oracle_matrix}). Two limits apply: the reference is a classifier rather than measured application slowdown, and ten repetitions bound the precision. The outcome is also expected by construction, because each search minimizes the same classifier that later serves as its reference; a classifier reference therefore cannot rank placements, which motivates the classifier-free yardstick of Section~\ref{sec:cost:truth}. The consequence for Section~\ref{sec:cost:tiers} is direct: the 45\% gap between canonical-7 and proxy-swap reflects what each classifier estimates and does not, on its own, show that the portable proxy yields better placements.

To separate them, the final placement of every simulation repetition is re-scored over the full 120-sample trace by every classifier in turn: each configuration's own classifier (self) and, in turn, each of the other two as the reference (oracle), at twenty repetitions per configuration (Figure~\ref{fig:oracle}). All three references score the same twenty placements per configuration, so the reference columns differ only in the classifier. Both scores use the same window, so they differ only in the classifier; because they score the final placement over the whole trace instead of averaging the scheduler's analysis intervals, which include the unoptimized initial placement, they differ from the indices of Figure~\ref{fig:tiers}: lower for canonical-7 and full-fingerprint, and slightly higher for proxy-swap (3959 against 3479). The canonical-7 classifier is pessimistic about its own placements: the full-fingerprint reference prices them 19\% lower (paired difference $-934$, 95\% CI $-1010$ to $-864$, permutation $p<0.001$). The proxy-swap classifier's self score does not differ from the full-fingerprint reference ($+64$, CI $-165$ to $+236$, permutation $p=0.64$)\oldval{at $n=10$ the same comparison read $+162$, CI $+58$ to $+283$, significant}. The full-fingerprint scores coincide by construction, which checks the re-scoring path. On the full-fingerprint reference, canonical-7 and proxy-swap placements are statistically indistinguishable (3880 versus 4022; difference $+142$, CI $-27$ to $+308$, Holm-corrected permutation $p=0.116$). Full-fingerprint placements score lower than both (3620; $-260$ versus canonical-7, CI $-417$ to $-94$, $p_{Holm}=0.009$; $-403$ versus proxy-swap, CI $-550$ to $-243$, $p_{Holm}=0.001$)\oldval{at $n=10$: $+135$ n.s.; $-237$ and $-372$}, but that comparison favours the full fingerprint by construction, since its search optimized against the same classifier that serves as the reference. Re-scoring with the canonical-7 and the proxy-swap classifiers as the reference shows that the ordering flips with the classifier and that the flip is now significant in both directions. On the canonical-7 reference, proxy-swap placements score 726 above canonical-7 ones (CI $+453$ to $+989$, $p_{Holm}=0.001$) and full-fingerprint placements are indistinguishable from canonical-7 ($+281$, CI $+34$ to $+561$, $p_{Holm}=0.111$); on the proxy-swap reference the sign reverses, proxy-swap placements scoring 734 below canonical-7 ones (CI $-1154$ to $-310$, $p_{Holm}=0.013$) and full-fingerprint placements worst ($+1555$ versus proxy-swap, CI $+861$ to $+2293$, $p_{Holm}=0.001$). The full fingerprint's penalty under the two five-class references has a mechanical cause: its regime workload, which those references cannot express, is relabelled as plain CPU in every sample. At twenty repetitions per cell, therefore, no reference-free ranking of these placements exists: each reference ranks its own configuration first in point estimate, and the canonical-7 versus proxy-swap comparison changes sign with the reference, significantly so under both five-class references (Figure~\ref{fig:oracle_matrix}). Two limits apply: the reference is a classifier rather than measured application slowdown, and twenty repetitions bound the precision. The outcome is also expected by construction, because each search minimizes the same classifier that later serves as its reference; a classifier reference therefore cannot rank placements, which motivates the classifier-free yardstick of Section~\ref{sec:cost:truth}. The consequence for Section~\ref{sec:cost:tiers} is direct: the 45\% gap between canonical-7 and proxy-swap reflects what each classifier estimates and does not, on its own, show that the portable proxy yields better placements.
